[S1] To onboard a trust, you need a certified copy of the trust deed, the list of trustees and beneficiaries, a photo ID for each trustee, and a source of wealth statement.

[S2] The service-desk team handles initial onboarding, while the kyc-ops team is responsible for KYC refreshes, onboarding documents, and address changes. Payments-ops is involved with wires, transfers, and holds, and compliance deals with fraud, sanctions, and suspicious activity.

[S1] Contoso Wealth client KYC standard / Periodic review cadence: Trusts and other entities are refreshed every year. When a review date passes, KYC status becomes expired.

[S1] Contoso Wealth client KYC standard / Expired KYC: An account with expired KYC is restricted to sell-only: no new purchases and no outgoing transfers until the refresh is completed by the kyc-ops team.

[S2] Contoso Wealth case handling guide / Routing rules: Questions about held or delayed wires go to payments-ops. KYC refreshes and address changes go to kyc-ops. Suspected fraud goes to compliance at sev1.

[S3] Contoso Wealth case handling guide / Teams: service-desk (first line), kyc-ops (KYC refreshes, onboarding documents, address changes), payments-ops (wires, transfers and holds), compliance (fraud, sanctions, suspicious activity).

Outgoing wires above 50,000 USD to a high-risk jurisdiction are held for compliance review. The review target is 2 business days.

[S2] Contoso Wealth client KYC standard / Expired KYC
An account with expired KYC is restricted to sell-only: no new purchases and no outgoing transfers until the refresh is completed by the kyc-ops team.

[S3] Contoso Wealth case handling guide / Severity
sev1: client funds at risk or suspected fraud. sev2: a held transfer past its review target, or a regulatory deadline. sev3: a standard client request. sev4: information only.
